 Trump bans some Canadian goods as trade war swells 







WASHINGTON, United States (AFP) — The White House ramped up its trade dispute with Canada late Tuesday by banning the import of certain products, including alcoholic beverages, and raising tariffs on other goods.

A range of Canadian products, from mattresses to motorboats and golf carts, will be subject to a 50-per cent surcharge beginning September 15, stated an executive order by President Donald Trump.

The import ban, which targets various alcoholic beverages as well as some dairy products like whey, will come into effect on September 29, according to other executive orders issued at the same time.

One of the statements of presidential action describes how certain Canadian products will no longer be subject to the 50 per cent tariffs that recently came into effect after bilateral trade negotiations collapsed last month. But the list of these products is significantly shorter, with toilet paper among them.

“President Trump is doing this to make sure, again, that we keep a level playing field, deter retaliation, and of course protect American production,” a senior administration official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.

The retaliation comes as Ottawa has just imposed new tariffs on US products in response to the duties announced by Washington on August 22.

The senior official said Canadians had been warned that their reaction would escalate the situation.

As justification for the ban on imports of alcohol from Canada, Trump cited what he called “discriminatory” provincial boycotts of US booze.

Since the start of Trump’s tariff offensive last year, Canadians have launched a massive boycott of US products: wines and spirits have disappeared from store shelves in most Canadian provinces, which hold a monopoly on their sale.

Earlier Tuesday, Trump had threatened to exclude Canadian products from a government procurement program “unless Canada restores full and fair reciprocity for American Farmers and Companies.”

In a social media post, Trump said he was directing officials “to REMOVE Canadian-origin products from GSA’s Multiple Award Schedules,” referring to a General Services Administration program for long-term contracts. Such schedules account for over $50 billion a year, Trump added.

US trade lawyer Ryan Majerus said the move could widen the scope of impacted goods beyond those hit by tariffs.

news.title: World News |  US Sanctions 27 Iranian Airlines with Third Country Firms Targeted
news.text:
Washington, DC [US], September 9 (ANI): The United States Department of the Treasury has placed 27 Iranian airlines on its Specially Designated Nationals List, effectively targeting every remaining commercial carrier in the country as part of an intensified pressure campaign against Tehran.

In a press statement issued on Tuesday, the department stated that "Iran's commercial airlines have long supported the Iranian regime's destabilising activities." It added that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has routinely utilised ostensibly private airlines to procure and transport weapons, as well as to ferry personnel.

Also Read | Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns, Warns AI Race Is Entering the 'Endgame' and Could 'Kill Us All'.

Washington initially sanctioned the Iranian carrier Mahan Air in October 2011, subsequently targeting several companies acting as its general sales agents on July 30.

The latest punitive measures also focus on "covert front companies, foreign intermediaries, and deceptive transhipment routes that Iran relies on to obtain US-origin aircraft and sensitive technology," the Treasury release noted.

Also Read | Donald Trump Bans Canadian Liquor, Dairy Goods as US-Canada Trade War Escalates.

Specifically, the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated four entities based in Türkiye, Malaysia, and Kazakhstan for operating as cargo service providers and general sales agents for Mahan Air. Furthermore, OFAC suspended authorisations that previously permitted overflights and allowed non-US airlines to operate US-origin or US-controlled commercial aircraft into Iran.

In a related move, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network under the Treasury Department issued an alert urging global financial institutions to report any procurement networks aiding the Iranian aviation sector. The Treasury release highlighted that Mahan Air acquired at least three Boeing 777 aircraft during the summer of 2026, which were covertly diverted through the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian responded on Tuesday, asserting that the nation will continue its resistance with strength until the "aggressors" are brought to complete regret.

Taking to the social media platform X, the Iranian leader emphasised the country's opposition to military conflict.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran has always been opposed to war and considered the preservation of the people's interests and ensuring the (West Asia) region's security to lie in refraining from warmongering," Pezeshkian stated.

"However, just as it has courageously risen to defend against aggression up to this day, Iran will continue this resistance with strength until the aggressors are brought to complete regret, and will remain the guardian of the rights of the great Iranian people," he added. (ANI)

news.title: Democrat Bekki Brewer Deletes Photo With '8647' Trump Sign
news.text: Missouri House candidate Bekki Brewer is pushing back against claims that an “8647” sign pictured alongside her advocated violence against President Donald Trump, saying it referred to the 25th Amendment and that she has “never and will never” support political violence. The photo shows Brewer, the Democratic candidate for Missouri House District 44, standing next to a man holding the sign. It went viral after the conservative social media account Libs of TikTok posted it Tuesday, writing the sign “symbolizes killing” Trump. The shorthand has become an anti-Trump protest slogan and has drawn federal scrutiny over whether it constitutes a threat against the president “The sign in the photo was referring to the 25th Amendment. It was not a call for political violence,” Brewer told Newsweek in a statement Tuesday. Brewer said the amendment provides a process for transferring presidential powers when a president is unable to carry out the duties of office, adding: “I fully support invoking that amendment when necessary.” Her post was later removed; Libs of TikTok shared a follow-up pointing out the deletion and tagging the FBI, as did several users in the replies. “I understand that people who see a photo online may not have the full context, but I’m not going to let a photo or the outrage surrounding it distract from why I decided to run,” she added. What Does “8647” Mean? The phrase “8647” combines “86,” long-standing slang for getting rid of or ejecting something, with “47,” a reference to Trump’s status as the 47th president. The phrase drew national attention in May 2025 after former FBI Director James Comey posted a photo showing seashells arranged on a beach to read “86 47.” Comey later deleted it, saying he was unaware of any violent meaning behind the numbers. A federal grand jury indicted him in April over the post. “Threatening the life of the President of the United States is a grave violation of our nation’s laws,” then-Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said following the indictment. The slogan has also prompted a federal investigation on the National Mall. In June, authorities discovered a massive “8647” marking etched into the grass near the Washington Monument. The Interior Department called it vandalism and said “any threat against the President is taken very seriously.” Later that month, “8647” was also scrawled onto a Texas exhibit at the Great American State Fair, prompting an investigation and its removal. A spokesperson for Texas Governor Greg Abbott told Newsweek the marking was “disgusting anti-Trump political graffiti.” Later Tuesday, Brewer addressed the photo in a Facebook post, writing that she would be at a community forum in Centralia this weekend to answer questions. Brewer said her campaign has been focused on how best to help the community and that she wants to keep the focus there. “I won’t allow a loud minority to steer the conversation away from this,” Brewer wrote. Brewer is the Democratic candidate for Missouri House District 44 in the November 3 general election. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Anna Commander and Gray R. Thomas
news.summary: The Missouri candidate said the “8647” sign referred to the 25th Amendment, not political violence.

news.title: World News | US Hits Canada with New Import Bans and Tariffs in Trade Stand-off
news.text:
By Reena Bhardwaj

Washington, DC [US], September 9 (ANI): The United States has announced a fresh round of trade measures against Canada, banning several categories of imports and reshuffling existing tariffs after Ottawa imposed its own retaliatory tariffs on American goods.

Also Read | Anthropic Researcher Jacob Coxon Resigns, Warns AI Race Is Entering the 'Endgame' and Could 'Kill Us All'.

Speaking to reporters on a background call, a senior US official said President Donald Trump had signed a series of proclamations under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, a rarely used law that lets Washington ban imports from countries it says are treating US trade unfairly.

The measures move on three fronts. Canadian dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles will now be barred from entering the US, with the bans due to take effect in roughly three weeks. Alongside this, Washington has reshuffled an earlier round of tariffs dated July 20: goods such as cement, road salt and certain medical supplies have been taken off that list, while new tariffs have been added on items including all-terrain vehicles, certain cheeses and motorboats. These changes take effect within a week. Separately, the administration has instructed federal procurement agencies to begin removing Canadian-origin goods from a government purchasing list worth an estimated USD 50 billion.

Also Read | Donald Trump Bans Canadian Liquor, Dairy Goods as US-Canada Trade War Escalates.

A previously announced threat to raise tariffs on Canadian cars and metals to 50 per cent from January 1 remains in place, officials confirmed.

According to the US side, Canada and China were the only two economies that responded to Washington's tariff push with retaliation of their own, rather than negotiating. Officials pointed out that dozens of other economies, Japan and the European Union among them, struck deals instead of retaliating.

The official argued that Canada's provinces had set a precedent by pulling US alcohol off shelves and restricting American firms from provincial procurement markets early in the trade dispute, and that this, rather than the tariffs themselves, is what triggered the ban authority under Section 338. 

For Indian exporters and trade watchers, the episode is a case study in how Washington's current trade strategy sorts countries into two camps: those that negotiate and those that retaliate. India has largely avoided the latter path, choosing instead to pursue a bilateral trade agreement with Washington even as tariff talks with the US have run in parallel with disputes over energy purchases from Russia.

Officials also downplayed concerns raised by some US lawmakers that the dispute could hurt Republican prospects in the coming midterm elections, saying the goods targeted make up a negligible share of overall US consumption.

The official also said the US had held what could be called constructive conversations with Canadian Minister Dominic LeBlanc in recent days, and expected further talks, though no timeline was given for resolving the dispute before the new bans take effect. Asked about a separate threat to restrict Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier, the official said no decision had yet been finalised. (ANI)

news.title: India takes muted approach to BRICS summit as geopolitical tensions rise
news.text:
Three years ago, New Delhi put on a spectacle when world leaders descended on India’s capital for the Group of 20 summit. Colorful murals of Indian mythology adorned the city alongside elaborate statues, floral arrangements and welcome billboards featuring Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In the weeks before Russia’s Vladimir Putin and other expected leaders like China’s Xi Jinping arrive in India for the BRICS Leaders’ Summit on Sept. 12-13, the mood in New Delhi has been relatively subdued. The occasional BRICS logo and welcome banners have only just started cropping up in the streets of the capital and around New Delhi’s main convention center, where the conference will take place.

Government officials in New Delhi have hardly mentioned the summit in their speeches, and the Ministry of External Affairs has published just 11 press releases with the BRICS tag between March 1 and Sept. 8, compared with 149 over the same period of time ahead of the G20 summit.

A muted BRICS build-up

Part of the reason for New Delhi’s muted approach is the diplomatic challenge it faces with US President Donald Trump, a vocal critic of BRICS. Trump sees the group — which expanded over the years from five to 10 full members now — as a threat to US geopolitical and economic influence. At the same time, the US is India’s biggest export market, and New Delhi is trying to keep relations with Trump on an even keel after a turbulent time last year marred by high tariffs.

“Turning BRICS into a show or spectacle would send a signal that India doesn’t want to send now,” said Karthik Nachiappan, non-resident senior fellow at the Institute of South Asian Studies in Singapore. “The low-key approach is to find a balance without overdoing things: host it competently, extract some value from the margins,” but don’t let BRICS become “an optic of India’s foreign policy.”

India’s Ministry of External Affairs didn’t respond to an emailed request for comment.

Balancing BRICS and global ties

India has traditionally viewed BRICS as a platform to amplify the voice of “emerging economies” and promote a more multi-polar global order. That balancing act has become harder as tensions among members deepen and Beijing’s economic and political weight gives it growing sway over the bloc.

Compared with India’s last BRICS in-person summit in 2016, this year’s gathering is notably subdued. Then, India held BRICS events across different states and planned more than 50 meetings between leaders both within and outside of government. New Delhi also organized business, academic, youth and cultural programs. By the end of the presidency a decade ago, India said it had held 115 BRICS-themed events.

In January this year, India unveiled marketing and a website for its BRICS presidency under the theme of “building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability.” Subsequent publicity has focused on the event’s technical aspects — meetings covering areas like energy, trade, technology and youth — rather than a broader national campaign promoting the gathering.

BRICS takes a lower-key approach

At the G20 summit, which is much bigger in scale, India put on an impressive show: New Delhi was festooned with elaborate murals, brightly lit fountains and ubiquitous G20 banners. Life-sized cut-outs of fang-baring langur monkeys adorned the city, a bid by officials to ward off New Delhi’s notorious macaques, in advance of arrivals by US President Joe Biden and leaders from Europe and Japan.

Many of the G20 posters, including those featuring a grinning Modi, still adorn the occasional New Delhi bus stop or public restroom today.

“The less fanfare around BRICS summit compared to the earlier G20 is likely due to the challenging geopolitical situation,” said Praveen Donthi, a senior analyst at the International Crisis Group. “The strained relations with the US, the war in the Middle East and the continued border dispute with China, which is the most dominant member of BRICS, likely contributed to the approach.”

Officials in New Delhi say the G20 and BRICS aren’t directly comparable. India has hosted BRICS summits before, whereas its G20 presidency in 2023 was a first. Since assuming the BRICS rotating presidency on Jan. 1, India has organized 350 lower-level meetings, including of foreign ministers, national security advisers and business leaders, according to the officials, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private.

“BRICS is certainly a platform where there have been too many challenges this year,” said Harsh Pant, vice president at the Observer Research Foundation, a New Delhi-based policy research group. “I don’t think New Delhi would particularly want to hype it up.”

news.title: US bans Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products as trade spat escalates
news.text:
The United States banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import on Tuesday, sharply escalating an already acrimonious trade spat.

The import bans, which go into effect on September 29 and were published on the White House's website, came after Canada's own retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect after midnight on Tuesday.

Those Canadian levies themselves followed 50% tariffs that the United States imposed on some $20 billion of Canadian goods last month, after several rounds of negotiations collapsed.

The breakdown has widened a rift between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the failed talks, spurred Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to urge a further shift away from Canada's biggest trading partner, and cast doubt on the viability of the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement.

"We have everything we need to pivot and prosper," Carney said on Tuesday in a video posted on YouTube.

Read moreCanada's counter-tariffs take effect on several US goods as trade war reignites

"That pivot will come at a cost. There's always a cost to action. But it doesn't come close to the cost of standing still," he said.

The US bans appeared to cover most alcohol products, including beer and various types of wine, whisky, bourbon, rum, vodka, vermouth, tequila, mezcal, and brandy. The dairy ban covers whey protein, invert molasses, cane molasses and non-alcoholic beer, per notices on the White House's website.

In addition to the import bans, various cheese products were added to a list of products subject to a 50% tariff, but not banned outright. Some paper, aluminium, wood, furniture, lighting and other products were also added to the list.

A US official said President Donald Trump's pre-existing threat to increase tariffs on Canadian autos from 25% to 50% on January 1 remained in effect. The official added that US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer had spoken with Dominic LeBlanc, Canada's minister responsible for bilateral US trade, over the past couple of days, and the pair were expected to speak again in the coming days to see if there was an alternative path for the two countries.

Read moreTrump threatens to ban Canadian Bombardier jets from US market

In a social media post on Tuesday night, LeBlanc criticised the latest US measures and said he was in contact with Greer regarding a path forward.

"As has been the case for the last 18 months, our first priority remains on protecting and supporting Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses from these unjustified actions," he wrote.

Ottawa strikes back

Ottawa's retaliatory measures, which in turn provoked Washington's move on Tuesday night, were designed to put economic and political pressure on Washington, Canadian government officials said.

Those counter-tariffs cover some $20 billion of US goods, with duties ranging from 15% to 50% across products from steel and furniture to clothing and electronics, and are expected to hit sectors in some competitive states such as Michigan and Ohio, ahead of US midterm elections in November.

While the tariffs affect a small amount of exports compared with total trade between the US and Canada, some analysts worry the standoff could destabilise the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the free-trade pact that succeeded NAFTA. Together they have underpinned commerce across North America for decades.
news.summary: The US and Canada escalated a bitter trade dispute on Tuesday, with Washington imposing new import bans on Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products as Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect.

news.title: SLEEPWALKING TO DISASTER
news.text:
Tatyana Deryugina & Yuriy Gorodnichenko

Twelve years ago, Ukraine was sleepwalking toward catastrophe. Now Europe is. Before 2014, Ukraine’s military had been hollowed out by decades of neglect and disarmament. That was a choice. Why spend scarce resources on defence when the 1994 Budapest Memorandum offered security assurances in exchange for Ukraine surrendering its nuclear arsenal? Why prepare for a conflict that the prevailing intellectual consensus said could never happen? Liberal democracy had triumphed, great-power conflict was a relic, and the arc of progress bent toward peace, liberalization, and economic convergence. Worse, Ukraine allowed Russia to penetrate its information space, promote pro-Kremlin narratives, cultivate political allies, and meddle in Ukraine’s elections. Under President Viktor Ya nukovych, a former Russian citizen served as minister of defence.

The army was sabotaged from within. Ukraine should have known better. The warning signs were there. Russia had invaded Georgia in 2008, demonstrating that it was prepared to use military force to prevent another former Soviet republic from escaping its orbit. Putin was already questioning whether Ukraine was a real country, describing parts of its territory as a “gift” from Russia. He publicly described Russians and Ukrainians as “one people,” and used energy and trade to gain political leverage. Yet the belief that Russia would go no further prevented decisive action. Then, in February and March 2014, Russia annexed Crimea without firing a shot because there was barely anyone to fire back (and those who might have helped urged Ukraine to stand down).

Shortly afterwards, Russia occupied parts of the Donbas. This time, Ukraine fought back, but from a position of profound weakness against a stronger and better-prepared adversary. Ukraine struggled to reach a consensus about what had happened and what must be done. While some called for mobilisation, many believed that the war was local and confi ned to a strip of territory in the east and a distant peninsula. The worst was over, they claimed: Putin had taken what he wanted. It followed that compromises, even if painful, could buy peace. Surely, the right leader could sit across the table from Putin and negotiate an end to the bloodshed. The election of Volodymyr Zelensky in 2019 partly reflected this yearning. Zelensky spoke of ending the war in Donbas, of talking directly to Russia, and of finding common ground.

Many Ukrainians wanted to believe that the problem could be talked away. Instead, on February 24, 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion, targeting Kyiv and seeking to decapitate the Ukrainian state. The war that was supposed to be local became existential. Europe’s resemblance to Ukraine’s trajectory is striking. The comparison is not exact: Europe is richer, more institutionally resilient, and still largely sheltered by NATO, at least in principle. But the similarity in habits of thought and action is close enough to be deeply troubling, as Germany’s pathetic reaction to a failed Russian drone attack at Leipzig airport amply demonstrates. After decades of peace, Europe has systematically dismantled its defence capabilities. NATO’s guideline of spending 2% of GDP on defence had, until recently, been treated as a ceiling rather than a floor.

For decades, Italy and Spain hovered around 1.5 per cent. Belgium and others trailed even further behind. Germany allowed the Bundeswehr to deteriorate to the point where soldiers trained with broomsticks instead of rifles and major weapons systems had readiness rates below 50 per cent. Europeans’ willingness to strengthen their defences via public-spending cuts or peacekeeping deployments in Ukraine is shockingly low. The mindset behind this neglect is familiar from Ukraine before 2014. Big wars cannot happen: we have the European Union, NATO, and nuclear deterrence. The United States will handle security. Defence spending is wasteful. Diplomacy and economic interdependence will keep the peace. Russia would never attack a major trading partner. Those assumptions have collapsed.

The US has signalled with increasing bluntness that the era of American security guarantees without European burden-sharing is over. President Donald Trump’s administration openly questions the value of NATO. Nuclear weapons do not deter subthreshold aggression (like drone and cyberattacks) or the use of coercion and subversion to erode sovereignty. What is striking in much of Europe is not just pacifi sm or poor readiness, but the lingering sense that even now the old rules will somehow reassert themselves. Europe is now facing its own warning signs. Russia is already waging what NATO calls a campaign of sabotage, cyberattacks, electronic interference, disinformation, and political influence across the continent. Russian drones and aircraft increasingly violate NATO airspace, while suspicious incidents around undersea cables and other infrastructure have forced NATO to strengthen their protection.

These provocations are deliberately below the threshold of war. That ambiguity enables Russia to probe European defences, test political resolve, and learn how much provocation the West will tolerate before responding. And, like Ukraine before 2014, Europe keeps finding reasons not to act. Across Europe, support for rearmament and for Ukraine remains politically contested. In Italy and Spain, voters resist higher defence spending. In France and Germany, influential voices frame urgency as overreaction (the far-right Alternative for Germany, which is likely to take power in Saxony-Anhalt, calls for a deal with Russia). In Slovakia, leaders have openly favoured accommodation with the Kremlin. Russia finances political parties, penetrates cultural institutions, and promotes disinformation throughout Europe. Across the continent, many argue that the war in Ukraine can be ended through negotiation if only Ukraine’s leaders would be more “realistic” about territorial concessions. Winston Churchill’s verdict on the catastrophic 1938 Munich Agreement is as relevant as ever: “You were given the choice between war and dishonor. You chose dishonor, and you will have war.”

Europe in 2026 can invest seriously in its own defence, accept the costs and trade-offs involved, and build credible deterrence. Or it can continue to underspend, hope that diplomacy alone will suffice, assume that US protection will always be available, and tell itself that the war in Ukraine is a local affair. But the price of appeasement is never paid by the politicians who choose expedience over vigilance. It is soldiers and civilians who bear the consequences. Europe still has time—provided by Ukraine, at extraordinary cost. The challenge is not merely to spend more, but to think differently: to accept that deterrence is not alarmism, preparedness is not provocation, and strength is often the precondition for peace.

Deryugina is Associate Professor of Finance at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Gorodnichenko is Professor of Economics at the University of California, Berkeley.

news.title: Free Flights and Free Hotels: Recruiters Line Up Crowds to Welcome Xi in Washington
news.text:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping is due at the White House on Sept. 24 for a state visit hosted by President Donald Trump.

In the weeks beforehand, recruiters working through Chinese-language group chats have been offering people free flights, hotel rooms, meals, and in one case $80 in cash to stand along the route with a flag.

Screenshots of those solicitations, obtained by The Epoch Times, describe an arrangement with three consistent features.

Costs are covered by the Chinese embassy and affiliated business groups; participation is presented as flag-waving hospitality rather than political work; and recruiting happens privately, in group chats and phone calls rather than public announcements.

Dissidents say that combination raises questions under federal laws governing people who act for foreign governments on U.S. soil.

One screenshot from a WeChat group says the event runs Sept. 22 to Sept. 26, is paid for by “the Chinese embassy and business associations,” and includes free airfare, food, and lodging.

A second message, signed by a chamber of commerce whose full name was withheld, recruits under the banner of “raising the flag in welcome,” promising covered meals, accommodation, and transportation plus a one-time $80 payment described as a “labor fee.”

Anyone under 70 may take part, and spots are allotted first come, first served.

A message circulating alongside the notice warned that U.S. law enforcement and intelligence agencies were likely taking note of the event, and joked that after inflation, $80 was “too low”—suggesting the money was being skimmed on its way down.

The Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

The recruiting is not confined to group chats.

A Chinese vice consul came to the hall of one community association in person in recent days and asked the group to join what he called the welcome event for “General Secretary Xi,” a figure at the association told The Epoch Times, speaking on condition of anonymity out of concern for retaliation.

The group declined; it is a century-old member of the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association, the Chinatown umbrella body that stayed firmly anti-communist after 1949.

A Chinese man in Los Angeles who also asked not to be named, citing his fear of reprisal, described a quieter version of the same approach.

Several years ago, when Xi visited San Francisco, a Southern California hometown association for people with roots in Taishan, Guangdong, sent a contingent to greet him.

He is a member and knew nothing in advance—he found out when photos from the scene and from a celebratory banquet appeared in the group chat.

Organizers keep these efforts out of open forums and approach specific people privately, he said, to make sure nothing goes wrong on the day.

Commenters circulating the notices said the crowds serve a purpose beyond decoration: when the motorcade passes, massed red flags, human walls, and loudspeakers cover the banners and chants of protesters, so the visiting leader sees and hears nothing.

The Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) requires anyone acting as an agent of a foreign government to register with the Justice Department and disclose the relationship, the activity, and the funding.

A separate criminal statute makes it an offense to act in the United States as an agent of a foreign government, under its direction, without notifying the Attorney General first.

Organizing people for political activity on the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) instructions without notifying the department is already a violation, he said, adding that he has turned screenshots and addresses over to federal agents.

Recruiters this year also ask participants to hand over identification.

Jie said that puts them at risk, since national ID numbers, passports, or U.S. driver’s licenses collected now could later be used to threaten exposure of their political activity or to pressure relatives in China.

He expects the money to work the way it did three years ago, when participants were promised $400 a day and got far less by the time it reached them.

Jie said he is watching to see whether the groups that ran the last operation turn up at all.

“Organizations like hometown associations that work for the CCP are very scared,” Jie said, adding that leaders once happy to be photographed at these events may stay away this time “because they’re genuinely afraid.”
news.summary: Notices circulated in Chinese-language group chats offer travel, meals, lodging, and cash for a five-day welcome in the US capital, residents said.

news.title: Minnesota Senate Race Deadlocked with Democrat and Republican, Poll Shows
news.text: A new poll shows Democrat Peggy Flanagan and Republican Michele Tafoya locked in a close race for Minnesota’s open U.S. Senate seat, with Flanagan holding a narrow 44 percent to 42 percent advantage among likely voters. The two-point gap puts the candidates within a statistical tie, underscoring how competitive the contest could become as the November midterms approach. The poll, conducted by TIPP/League of American Workers from August 31 to September 2 among 1,201 likely voters, also found 4 percent supporting other candidates, while 2 percent said someone else and 8 percent were not sure. The survey comes shortly after both candidates secured their party nominations last month, setting up a general election contest for the seat being vacated by Democratic Senator Tina Smith. The poll has a margin of error of 3 percent. The League of American Workers is not formally affiliated with the Republican Party, but it is a conservative advocacy organization led by former Trump adviser Steve Cortes. Meanwhile, midterm elections are commonly viewed as a test of the political environment facing the party in power, and the president's party has historically lost seats during midterm elections. Republicans currently hold a narrow majority in the House and Senate, and The Cook Political Report currently rates the race as likely Democrat. Former Vice President Kamala Harris also won the state by roughly 4 points in the 2024 presidential election over President Donald Trump. Flanagan campaign spokesperson Lexi Byler told Newsweek via email on Tuesday when reached for comment about the new poll, "Michele Tafoya would be nothing but a loyal soldier to Donald Trump. She supports his ICE and mass deportation agenda that led to two Minnesotans being killed, defended January 6 rioters who assaulted police officers and tried to overturn a free and fair election, and supports Trump’s reckless tariffs that are hammering farmers and driving up prices for everyone. Tafoya even told Minnesotans to just 'keep a stiff upper lip' with the higher prices due to Trump’s illegal war in Iran and praised the One Big Beautiful Bill that is ripping health care away from hundreds of thousands of Minnesotans." "Michele Tafoya is fighting for what Trump wants, Peggy Flanagan is fighting for what working families need – Minnesotans know that and it’s why they will choose Peggy Flanagan in November," the statement concluded. Newsweek reached out to Tafoya's campaign via email on Tuesday for comment, and while she did not respond before publication time, she responded to the poll on X, saying, "Our race is in play! Minnesotans are fed up with billions in taxpayer dollars being stolen while the people in charge refuse to take responsibility. Peggy Flanagan is the sitting lieutenant governor while criminals were stealing billions from Minnesota taxpayers. She doesn’t get to walk away from that record. Minnesotans deserve accountability. They deserve leadership. And they deserve better. This race is wide open. Let’s win it!" What To Know Flanagan, Minnesota's lieutenant governor, entered the general election as the Democratic nominee after defeating Representative Angie Craig in the party's primary. Flanagan’s defeat of Craig marked a victory for the Democratic Party’s more progressive wing, which has seen several candidates prevail in recent primaries. Flanagan was considered the more progressive candidate in the contest and received backing from Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders and Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar, making the race another example of the ongoing divide between progressive and moderate Democrats. Tafoya, a former longtime NFL sideline reporter, won the Republican nomination and is seeking to turn her name recognition and political outsider profile into a statewide victory. The race has drawn national attention as Republicans look to make gains in Minnesota, even though Democrats have maintained a strong statewide advantage in recent elections. The latest numbers are particularly notable because earlier polling also showed Flanagan ahead, although by a somewhat larger margin. The new survey suggests Tafoya may have narrowed the gap as the general election campaign gets underway. Still, a two-point advantage is not enough to establish a clear favorite, particularly with two months remaining before Election Day. According to the poll, Flanagan has more of the Gen-Z, Millennial, female, Black and Hispanic vote. Tafoya has more support from those age 45-years-old and up, men, and white likely voters. Both have 37 percent of the independent vote. Among registered voters Flanagan also has a 2-point lead over Tafoya with 40 percent to 38 percent. That questioned polled 1,494 registered voters and has a margin of error of 2.7 percent. Tafoya has a 34 percent favorable rating compared to a 30 percent unfavorable rating, the poll shows, while 36 percent have no opinion. Flanagan's favorability rating is 39 percent compared to a 34 percent unfavorable rating and 28 percent have no opinion. The survey also asked respondents about Flanagan's position on gender transitions for minors and their potential support. No similar or direct policy question was asked about Tafoya. For now, the latest poll points to a race that could be competitive, with Flanagan and Tafoya separated by just two percentage points and both campaigns facing an opportunity to persuade the relatively small share of voters who have yet to settle on a candidate. What Prediction Markets Show According to Kalshi on Monday afternoon, Flanagan has a 90.5 percent chance of winning to Tafoya's 9.5 percent chance. Polymarket shows a similar finding on Monday afternoon, with Flanagan having a 94 percent chance to Tafoya's 8 percent. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Gray R. Thomas

news.title: Donald Trump Bans Canadian Liquor, Dairy Goods as US-Canada Trade War Escalates
news.text:
Washington, September 9: US President Donald Trump has ordered bans on a broad range of Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motorcycles as his administration escalated its trade confrontation with Canada. The import bans will take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern time on September 29, according to a series of White House proclamations. Canadian goods imported before that date but not cleared for consumption will remain subject to the existing 50 per cent duty.

A senior administration official told reporters on Tuesday (local time) that the measures were designed to counter Canadian retaliation, protect American production and restore what the White House considers a level playing field. US-Canada Trade War: Donald Trump Announces 50% Tariffs on Autos and Steel From January 2027.

The official said the import bans would affect Canadian trade valued in the “single-digit billions”. Changes to the existing tariff list would not significantly alter the roughly $20 billion in trade covered by those duties.

“The actual economics of it is much more challenging for Canada than it is for us,” the official said, arguing that the measures covered about 0.1 per cent of overall US consumption. The prohibited alcoholic beverages include packaged beer, sparkling wine, cider, sake, whisky, bourbon, rum, gin, vodka, tequila, brandy, liqueurs and other spirits. Donald Trump Says Canada Cannot Survive Without US As Trade Tensions Escalate.

Trump also barred designated Canadian dairy-related goods, including whey protein concentrates, modified whey, fluid whey, dried whey and several forms of molasses. Non-alcoholic beer is also covered. A separate proclamation bars Canadian motorcycles and cycles fitted with engines exceeding 800cc.

Alongside the bans, Trump modified the range of Canadian products subject to the existing 50 per cent duties. Those changes will take effect on September 15.

The revised list adds several categories of paper, iron and steel structures, aluminium products, metal fittings, golf carts, small motor vehicles, outboard motorboats, furniture, mattresses and lamps. It also adds certain cheeses not made from cow’s milk.

The administration removed salt, Portland cement, refined lead, certain household paper products, switchgear assemblies and some fishing rod parts and accessories from the tariff list.

The official said the changes reflected feedback from businesses after the earlier duties took effect. Some products were removed because parts of the United States had a unique dependence on Canadian supplies that could not easily be replaced.

The official also confirmed that Trump’s plan to raise tariffs on Canadian vehicles to 50 per cent on January 1 remained in effect. “The President's position on autos going up to 50 per cent on January 1st, that remains, that remains in effect,” the official said.

The White House, at the same time, is open to negotiations. The official said conversations with Canadian officials over the past several days had been constructive.

“Yes, that's always a possibility,” the official said when asked whether an alternative agreement could be reached. Another discussion with Canada was expected within days.

Trump first imposed the additional duties under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 through proclamations issued on July 20. Their implementation was briefly suspended after Canada expressed a commitment to address the disputed measures.

The suspension expired on August 22 after the White House said Canada had failed to remove them. Section 338 allows the President to impose duties of up to 50 per cent and, under specified conditions, bar goods from a country that maintains discrimination against US commerce.

(The above story first appeared on LatestLY on Sep 09, 2026 07:49 AM IST. For more news and updates on politics, world, sports, entertainment and lifestyle, log on to our website latestly.com).
news.summary: The United States has announced new import bans on selected Canadian dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles, escalating its trade dispute with Canada after Ottawa imposed retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars worth of American goods.

news.title: Michael Goodwin: Mamdani’s toxic Ground Zero blame game just latches on to still-open 9/11 wounds to boost himself
news.text:
The 25th anniversary of the horrific events of 9/11 will be, as it must, a somber reminder of those we lost on the deadliest day in American history.

The reading of the names of the fallen and the tolling of the bells are rites that never grow old. They vividly remind New Yorkers and the world of the ultimate price 2,753 innocent people paid that day in the Twin Towers, on the ground, in nearby buildings and in the two hijacked jet liners.

Nearly 200 other innocents perished when a third hijacked plane smashed into the Pentagon, and 40 passengers were killed when they heroically fought terrorists on a fourth jet that crashed in Shanksville, Pa.

The Manhattan ceremony at the site known around the world as Ground Zero will properly salute the undaunted courage of hundreds of firefighters and police officers — the Bravest and the Finest — who perished while valiantly trying to save others.

National unity

Remembered, too, will be the crews and passengers of the two giant airliners seized by terrorists and flown into the buildings.

The immediate impact was an ocean of shock and anger that quickly forged a rarely seen national unity. A fervor of patriotism previously reserved for world wars and national calamities swept the nation.

Yet as time passes, events shaped by the attacks and the aftermath also must be included to gain a more complete picture of that historic day.

Most tragically, a total of 9,677 first responders and survivors have died from 9/11-related illnesses, according to federal data, meaning those deaths far exceed the number of fatalities from the actual attacks.

Most have died from various cancers related to the toxins released by the collapsing and burning of the skyscrapers. Reports say that in total, more than 57,000 cases of cancer that can be traced to the aftermath have been documented.

Just as the attack dramatically heightened the national awareness of Islamist terrorism and led to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, the devastating health fallout continues to roil our society.

In hindsight, it was inevitable that the spirit of unity in Washington and New York would give way to a politics scrambled by different -reactions to the attacks on America.

The word “homeland” was not commonly used until then, but events gave birth just a few days later to the federal Department of Homeland Security. It was formally created by a wave of bipartisanship in Congress as a stand-alone agency the following year.

Its mission has grown dramatically, and is now described on its website as being “to secure the nation from the many threats we face.” It has some 260,000 employees covering aviation and border security, emergency response as well as cybersecurity.

Yet increasingly, the soaring cancer rates and related findings in and around Ground Zero have sparked pointed questions about what the various levels of government knew and when they knew it.

Reckless claim

The questions are legitimate and deserve answers. But what is illegitimate is the reckless, unproven claim that Rudy Giuliani and every mayor since him has been part of a conspiracy to hide deadly truths from the public.

That was the tone and substance of Mayor Mamdani’s rant at City Hall Tuesday when he announced the creation of a public portal and the release of 170,000 pages of post-9/11 information.

“People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air. And then, when they began to contend with the symptoms of the illnesses that followed, the government that had not hesitated to send them into harm’s way was nowhere to be found,” he declared.

It sounds as if, had he been mayor, the ruins would still be there and no rebuilding of the site would have taken place.

As always, his “facts” are distorted by ignorance and bias. The smoldering pile was obviously unhealthy, but state-of-the-art breathing-protection equipment was scarce for the scale of the operation, and some uniformed searchers, in their grief and fury, refused to use the equipment that was available.

For Mamdani and his socialist troops, the sudden concern is the political equivalent of a lawyer who chases an ambulance after an accident in the lust for a big payday.

Because he is the ultimate outsider now running the inside, it is impossible to escape the suspicion that Mamdani is latching on to the open wounds of 9/11 to boost his sketchy standing.

Consider that he is the subject of a petition signed by more than 102,000 people urging him to stay away from Friday’s ceremony.

The signers include many who lost friends and family in the attack and aftermath.

The mayor has only himself to blame for the opposition, in that he came of age politically in the anti-police wave that started under Barack Obama’s presidency. Mamdani swallowed and repeated the “all cops are racist” smear, hook, line and sinker.

And at just age 34, the city’s first Muslim mayor did not help his cause by hanging out with Hasan Piker, the radical social media star who declared that “America deserved 9/11.”

Called on his association, Mamdani suddenly declared Piker’s comments “objectionable and reprehensible.”

Damning predecessors

Still, his glib damning of all recent mayors omits any federal responsibilities on air-quality issues, which rests with the Environmental Protection Agency.

If documents were hidden by the feds since 9/11, that would span the terms of every president, from George W. Bush to Donald Trump, and including Obama and Joe Biden.

And what about Albany? Mamdani’s new best friend, Gov. Hochul, has been in office for five years. Are her hands clean on the charge of concealed air quality findings?

More likely, his Tuesday speech was just another partisan attack meant to detract attention from Mamdani’s own thin record on terrorism and his hatred of Israel. Whatever the world’s problems, he is among those who instinctively blame America first.

His experience and ideology blind him to a fear that many New Yorkers had for days and even years after 9/11. It often seemed as if another, even larger attack on the city was inevitable.

I was among those people and, in a private conversation, confessed my fear to Ray Kelly, during his term as Mayor Bloomberg’s police commissioner. Kelly was taken aback, looked sternly at me and said, “I don’t believe that. It’s not inevitable.”

I was embarrassed, then relieved to realize how dedicated he and so many others were in making sure there was no second -attack.

Thankfully, they succeeded and there is every reason to believe that Kelly’s resolute attitude continues at Police Plaza under his protégée, current Commissioner Jessica Tisch.

Is City Hall on the same page? I wish it were but I fear it is not.
news.summary: The 25th anniversary of the horrific events of 9/11 will be, as it must, a somber reminder of those we lost on the deadliest day in American history.

news.title: Veterans Group 'Appalled' by Trump's Plan to Build Arch on 'Burial Ground'
news.text: Veterans opposed to President Donald Trump’s proposed 250-foot triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery are stepping up efforts to block the project, less than two weeks before excavation work at the site is slated to begin. The arch is one of several construction and renovation projects undertaken or proposed by the Trump administration as part of a broader effort to beautify and renovate parts of Washington. Trump has said the arch, in particular, is intended to honor veterans. “It’s called the Triumphal Arch. It’s in honor of the veterans,” Trump has said. Concerns About Triumphal Arch VoteVets, a Democratic veterans organization, posted a new video Tuesday featuring veterans and Gold Star families raising concerns about the project’s potential impact on Arlington National Cemetery. “This isn’t about politics. It’s about letting a burial ground stay a burial ground,” the organization wrote in a post on X. She pointed to the proposed observation deck, saying: “We don't need tourists overlooking funerals. I'm just appalled.” Retired Army Major General Paul Eaton, whose father was killed in action during the Vietnam War and is buried at Arlington, raised concerns about the arch disrupting the sight line between the Lincoln Memorial and the cemetery. Eaton called its proposed placement “entirely inappropriate” and said it “borders on sacrilege.” Newsweek has reached out to the White House for comment. Has Construction Started on Trump's Arch? Interior Secretary Doug Burgum announced on September 3 that excavation work for the proposed Great Triumphal Arch and Military Observation Deck at Memorial Circle would begin within two weeks. Burgum called the project “one of the Great Pieces of American Architecture,” saying it would honor the “history” and “significance” of Arlington Cemetery. What Legal Challenge Does the Arch Face? The following day, on September 4, a group of Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian suing over the proposed triumphal arch sought an emergency court order to halt work on the project. Veterans Michael Lemmon, Shaun Byrnes, and Jon Gundersen, and architectural historian Calder Loth, argued that the administration could not move forward with the project without congressional approval. Construction of the arch would “destroy this unobstructed view and the symbolic connection” between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington House that holds “deep meaning to them, thereby degrading plaintiffs’ future visits,” the filing states. The plaintiffs first sued the Trump administration over the project in February. On Tuesday, Democratic Representative Chellie Pingree urged House Speaker Mike Johnson to file a lawsuit on behalf of Congress to block the administration from moving forward with the arch. “Congress has neither appropriated funding nor granted authority for this project under the Commemorative Works Act,” Pingree wrote in a letter to Johnson. “I am asking you to take all necessary steps to file suit immediately, while there is still ground left to save.” Pingree is the ranking member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies. What Trump Has Said While speaking with reporters in April, Trump was asked about the February lawsuit and concerns that the arch would obstruct the view between Arlington National Cemetery and the Lincoln Memorial. “You got to be kidding,” Trump responded. “This was approved 100 years ago,” he said, referring to earlier plans for monumental structures at the site that were never built. “Our veterans are the ones that should like it,” Trump said. “It’s called the Triumphal Arch. It’s in honor of the veterans.” In a February interview with NBC News, Trump said the arch is part of a broader effort to bring “glamour,” “prestige” and “beauty” back to the country, noting that other major cities have arches while Washington does not. “We’re doing one that will be more magnificent and larger than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris,” Trump said, calling the Paris monument “incredible." “We’re going to do one that’s going to top it.” Where Would the Arch Be Located? The proposed arch would be located at Memorial Circle on Columbia Island, at the western end of Arlington Memorial Bridge between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. It won't be inside Arlington National Cemetery, but adjacent to its main entrance. What Is the Triumphal Arch? The arch would stand 250 feet tall and is designed as a monumental gateway celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence. In Tuesday’s video, Charles Birnbaum, founding president and CEO of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, said a monument of that height would alter the relationship between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. “It will alter that hallowed ground and that feeling and association that everyone has when they experience the cemetery,” Birnbaum said. The video also points to plans for construction to take place up to 20 hours a day for as long as three years, noting that someone is buried at Arlington “every weekday.” The group called for the public to weigh in by the end of September ahead of what it says is an upcoming vote by the National Capital Planning Commission, which granted preliminary approval to the project in July but has not yet given final approval. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Samantha Beech and Gray R. Thomas
news.summary: Veterans and Gold Star families raise concerns about the monument's impact on Arlington ahead of scheduled excavation work.

news.title: Slovak FM calls for more active EU role in Ukraine peace efforts
news.text: Digital Desk | Bratislava, Sep 9 (IANS) European Union (EU) leaders should have played a more active role in seeking a diplomatic solution to the conflict in Ukraine, Slovak Foreign and European Affairs Minister Juraj Blanar said in an interview with TASR TV. Blanar said the United States is now playing a significantly greater role in the peace process, while Europe has provided substantial financial support to Ukraine. "At present, we basically don't have a seat at the table. We are simply paying all the costs associated with it," Blanar said. According to data released by the European External Action Service, since the start of the war, the EU and our member states have made available to Ukraine over 226 billion US dollars in financial, military, humanitarian, and refugee assistance, reports Xinhua news agency. Blanar said Slovakia could find common ground with its partners in the Visegrad Four (V4), comprising the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia, on the need for a more active EU role in the peace process, although the four countries have different views on how to achieve a ceasefire. He noted that Slovakia, Hungary and the Czech Republic would not participate in guarantees for a 90 billion euro (104.5 billion US dollars) loan to Ukraine, while Poland had decided to do so. "Despite having different views, we are still able to discuss these issues together," Blanar said. Slovakia assumed the one-year V4 presidency on July 1 this year. According to Blanar, Slovakia is preparing for a meeting of the Slovak and Ukrainian governments, which is expected to take place in Lviv, Ukraine, but the date has not yet been decided. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump on Tuesday held a telephone conversation that was "constructive and very frank," Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said. Ushakov said the call lasted exactly one hour, adding that during the conversation, Putin stressed that Russia has no hostile intentions toward European countries. "Against the backdrop of speculation alleging that Russia holds hostile intentions toward European states, it was emphasised that we do not harbour any aggressive plans against Europe whatsoever. The circulated myths about a Russian threat serve as a cover for European nations to ramp up support for Ukraine and increase their own military spending," Ushakov said. Ushakov said Trump, for his part, stressed the need to end the Ukraine conflict, a move that would immediately open broad and promising prospects for the full restoration of Russia-US relations. The two sides agreed to continue efforts to resolve humanitarian issues, including the exchange of detained and convicted individuals.

news.title: US Government suspends Cognizant’s PERM applications for foreign workers
news.text:
The United States Department of Labour (DOL) has suspended PERM applications for US-headquartered IT services firm Cognizant, citing possible fraud involving the employment-linked immigration programme.

What is PERM?

PERM, or the Permanent Labour Certification, allows employers to hire a foreign worker to work permanently in the United States. Unlike the H1B programme, which grants the employee a temporary work visa, PERM is the first step towards a permanent green card.

To obtain the certification, the employer must first ‘test the labour market’ and certify there are no qualified U.S. workers available for the job. They must also show that hiring a foreign worker will not lower the wages or working conditions.

DOL announces Cognizant suspension

Anthony D’Esposito, Inspector General of the Department of Labour, announced in a post on X on Tuesday night.

“Fighting fraud is a team sport. Cognizant’s PERM filings are suspended. The Department of Labour alongside the White House Fraud Task Force is on the hunt. We are following facts, fraud and finances. Handcuffs await,” the tweet read.

Cognizant has not yet responded to businessline’s query on the issue as of the time of filing the report.

IT companies rely on PERM

IT service companies have long used the PERM programme to sponsor employment-based green cards for Indian national employees.

In the first three quarters of FY26 (US Federal Year format from October-September), a total of 104,028 permanent labour certifications were issued, out of which the Professional, Scientific and Technical Services, which includes IT service employees, accounted for 28,425 certifications or 27.3 per cent.

While the DOL no longer publishes country-- and company-wise data on the number of PERM certifications, Indians accounted for 65,095 in FY16, when the data was last released.

Multiple IT service companies, including Cognizant, Wipro, Infosys, and HCL, featured among the top ten employers with PERM certifications at that time.

US steps up immigration scrutiny

The suspension of Cognizant’s PERM applications by the US government comes amid a wider crackdown on alleged visa fraud and exploitation of employment-related immigration programs.

Esposito said in July of this year that the Department of Labour will launch an investigation into the alleged misuse of the employment visa, along with labour trafficking and other fraudulent labour practices. Cognizant was then mentioned as one among the companies under scrutiny.

The US government had previously sought to make the H-1B visa regime more stringent when President Donald Trump signed an order imposing a one-time $100,000 fee on new petitions. However, a federal judge struck down the order in June of this year.

Published on September 9, 2026
news.summary: The move adds to growing scrutiny of employment-linked immigration programmes as the US government investigates alleged misuse and fraudulent labour practices

news.title: Trump Launches Back-to-Back Attacks on ‘3rd Rate’ Kaitlan Collins and ‘Unattractive’ Maggie Haberman
news.text:
Donald Trump once again publicly criticized CNN’s Kaitlan Collins and the New York Times’ Maggie Haberman, launching back-to-back attacks against the female journalists on social media.

On Tuesday, the president kicked off his renewed attacks on female journalists by zeroing in on Collins on Truth Social, where he blasted her as a “3rd rate” anchor.

“Very dumb and unhappy Fake News CNN ‘reporter,’ Kaitlan Collins (really low ratings, also!), had a panel where discussions were all FICTION AND LIES,” Trump wrote on Tuesday. “You would think that CNN, which is suffering terribly in the TV Ratings, would get rid of their 3rd rate ‘anchors,’ and try to bring credibility back to their once storied network. It is fading FAST! See you all at the Republican National Convention tomorrow night!!!”

He then followed this post up with a scathing rebuke of Haberman, who he suggested “knows less about me than the average reporter ‘on the beat.’” We should note, Haberman received critical acclaim for her 2026 book with Jonathan Swan, “Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump.”

Trump once more took umbrage with the New York Times’ story that claimed he planned to skip a 9/11 memorial service at Ground Zero because he would be unable to give a speech. Haberman was one of four reporters who contributed to the story.

“Maggot Hagerman continues to say that I did not go to the New York World Trade Center event, but the Pentagon instead, because they wouldn’t let me speak in New York,” he wrote in a separate Truth Social post. “Maggot knows that this is a lie! I have been to the New York solemn ceremony numerous times, and nobody speaks. It is a stated fact that, ‘Politicians and public officials are not permitted to deliver speeches or remarks at the official September 11 anniversary remembrance ceremony at the World Trade Center site in New York.’” 

“Certainly I would not want to violate that, even if I could,” he continued. “I speak enough, and it just so happens that the strong request was made for me to be at the Pentagon instead, with VP Vance handling our Administration’s representation in New York. Hagerman, unattractive both inside and out, fully knows that her story is made up. She knows less about me than the average reporter ‘on the beat.’ I haven’t spoken to her in a long time, and certainly there was no ‘fact checking’ for her story — There never is!”

As Trump went on, he called on Haberman to “reveal her sources,” claiming that she couldn’t because “they don’t exist.”

“Fake News is getting worse and worse in the U.S.A.” he bemoaned. “It’s very important to comment so that people understand what liars and scoundrels these so-called ‘journalists’ are. They’re angry, and sick, over the fact that I won the Presidential Election three times!”

In this same post, Trump took issue with a New York magazine story that tackled his 9/11 claims, writing, “The Failing New York Magazine wrote a story that I wasn’t down at the World Trade Center after the Tragedy of September 11th, because nobody saw me there. Well, I don’t think I would be the first thing on anyone’s mind but, I was there, obviously not on the same day as the collapse, but shortly thereafter, with a large group of Construction Workers.”

“I discussed it today during my Remarks on the Ellipse, in Washington, D.C., for Tunnel to Towers,” he added. “Everything I said was exactly accurate and, to prove the point, I am attaching clips of me there with numerous of my people, including my then Head of Security, Matthew Calamari, who has confirmed that very sad trip to Lower Manhattan, many times, to many different Journalists, but it’s a story that just won’t die. The Fake News doesn’t want to listen, even when they know their story is false. That’s why their approval ratings are at an All Time LOW, but mine are VERY HIGH!”

He then demanded that both Haberman and the New York Magazine retract their statements about him.

Of course, this is not the first time that Trump has taken aim at the press or female reporters, as Kristen Holmes, Collins, Kristen Welker, Catherine Lucey, Jessica Tarlov and Shannon Bream have all faced his wrath these last 19 months. 

In fact, earlier this summer, Trump called out Collins at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, where he compared her to trans actress and influencer Dylan Mulvaney in his speech. Additionally, just last month, he labeled Haberman as a “fake reporter” over the aforementioned 9/11 memorial story – which the Times defended was “based on information from multiple people with knowledge of the discussions and planning around New York’s Sept. 11 ceremony.”

Representatives for CNN, the New York Times and New York Magazine did not immediately respond to TheWrap’s request for comment regarding Trump’s Tuesday posts.
news.summary:
"Fake News is getting worse and worse in the U.S.A.," the president writes

news.title: US Strikes 5 Iranian Oil Tankers Near Kharg Island After Iran Targets Navy Ship
news.text:
The United States has destroyed five Iranian oil tankers near Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf after Iranian forces launched ballistic missile attacks targeting an American Navy warship, marking a major escalation in the continuing conflict between Washington and Tehran, TOI reported.

U.S. Central Command said the latest military action followed what it described as failed Iranian attacks on American naval forces. The strikes came just days after U.S. forces targeted three other Iranian crude carriers in the region. Donald Trump Weighs Ending Iran War as Pentagon Extends Troop Deployment.

US Strikes 5 Iranian Oil Tankers Near Kharg Island

CENTCOM forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers, Sept. 8, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days. The U.S. warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and… pic.twitter.com/Gi8a2tloN1
— U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) September 8, 2026

Five Iranian Tankers Targeted

According to U.S. military officials, American forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers on Tuesday following missile attacks attributed to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The vessels were identified in reports as the Kivik, Charminar, Horizon 1, Riesco and Derya. U.S. officials said the tankers were linked to a network that Washington alleges helps finance the IRGC.

The strikes reportedly took place near Kharg Island, one of Iran's most important oil export hubs in the Persian Gulf. Reports said crews were directed to evacuate before the vessels were struck. Donald Trump Warns US Could Strike Iran’s Deeply Buried ‘Pickaxe Mountain’ Nuclear Facility.

Iran Responds With Further Threats

Following the U.S. strikes, tensions continued to rise as Iran reportedly launched missiles towards U.S.-linked targets in Jordan. Air defence systems intercepted the attacks, with no casualties immediately reported. Iran also issued threats against oil shipping in the Gulf, including vessels connected to Kuwait and Bahrain, while announcing plans for a maritime exclusion zone around the Strait of Hormuz.

Latest Strike Follows Earlier Tanker Attacks

The latest action came after U.S. forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on September 5 following missile attacks targeting an American aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer.

U.S. Central Command said at the time that Iranian missiles failed to hit the Navy vessels and no American personnel were injured. Two Iranian crude carriers were permanently disabled, while a third was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman. The new operation brings the number of Iranian tankers targeted by U.S. forces in the latest round of hostilities to eight.

Concerns Over Oil Supply and Strait of Hormuz

The escalation has raised fresh concerns over energy supplies and maritime security in the Middle East. Kharg Island is a key hub for Iranian crude exports, while the nearby Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most strategically important shipping routes for oil and liquefied natural gas.

The conflict and growing threats to shipping have pushed oil prices higher, with crude approaching $100 per barrel in recent trading. Continued disruption in the Gulf could further affect global energy markets and shipping routes.

US-Iran Tensions Continue to Escalate

The latest exchange reflects a continuing cycle of military retaliation between the United States and Iran, with both sides increasing pressure through military operations and threats against shipping. Washington has combined military action with additional economic sanctions targeting Iran, while Tehran has warned of further retaliation against U.S. interests and vessels operating in the region.

With attacks involving warships, oil tankers and military installations continuing across the region, concerns are growing that further escalation could pose a wider threat to Gulf security and global energy supplies.

news.summary: US military launched strikes on five Iranian crude oil tankers near Kharg Island and in the Gulf of Oman, according to a U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) report released Tuesday. The offensive comes after Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted an American Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over two days.

news.title: Berlin slams Kiev for not spending aid cash on German guns
news.text:
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has criticized Kiev for failing to spend enough of its Western-provided procurement money on German weapons, arguing that Berlin’s massive support for Ukraine should at least benefit its defense industry.

Germany is one of Ukraine’s largest bilateral supporters, having provided or earmarked more than €43 billion ($50 billion) in “civilian” assistance and around €58 billion in military aid since the conflict escalated in 2022.

“We are now the strongest supporter of Ukraine in terms of financial and military support. And naturally, the German defense industry must benefit from this,” Wadephul told Bild in an interview published on Tuesday.

The minister said he had raised the issue directly with Vladimir Zelensky during his visit to Kiev last month.

“We stand by you, we support you. But I also have to explain this to German taxpayers, and the very least you can do is to involve the German defense industry in all procurement measures,” Wadephul recalled telling the Ukrainian leader.

“At the moment, we are not entirely satisfied with the level of orders in Germany,” he added, saying Kiev had been asked to review its purchases and ensure that the situation “gets better.”

Germany’s demands that the money spent on Kiev flow back to its own arms makers mirror US President Donald Trump’s approach to Ukraine aid. Since returning to the White House, Trump has largely shifted the financial burden of supplying American weapons to European NATO members and Canada. Under the PURL mechanism, the bloc’s members now pay Washington for US-made arms that are then delivered to Kiev.

Moscow has repeatedly criticized the unprecedented military buildup by Germany and the wider EU under the pretext of alleged Russian threat. President Vladimir Putin said in June that Western governments were no longer concealing their intentions and were “openly saying that they are preparing for war with us.”

Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has warned that Germany and the rest of Europe under their current leadership are “transforming into a Fourth Reich” and seeking to fight Russia “to the last Ukrainian.”

Berlin has simultaneously stepped up pressure on Ukrainian men of military age living in Germany to return home “without coercion.” Wadephul backed calls by Bavarian leader Markus Söder and suggested that German authorities could provide Kiev with information identifying Ukrainians receiving welfare benefits or holding registered residency status so they could be “contacted” for mobilization. Germany has separately backed stripping newly arriving draft-age Ukrainian men of the automatic temporary-protection privileges granted to refugees.
news.summary:
Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has criticized Kiev for failing to spend enough of its Western-provided procurement money on German weapons

news.title: World News | US-Canada Trade War: Trump Orders Import Bans and Revised Tariffs on Vehicles, Alcohol, and Dairy
news.text:
Washington, DC [US], September 9 (ANI): The ongoing trade dispute between the US and Canada has intensified as President Donald Trump has issued five presidential directives targeting Canadian imports through import exclusions and adjusted tariff structures, citing persistent trade discrimination by Ottawa.

The White House stated the executive actions follow a breakdown in bilateral negotiations after Canada failed to honour commitments to eliminate discriminatory trade measures.

Also Read | Channel 4 Layoffs: Broadcaster To Cut 300 Jobs in Largest Restructuring in History.

The five directives establish specific enforcement actions and policy changes across three affected commercial sectors:

The first directive excludes certain Canadian motor vehicles and automotive components from importation into the United States. The White House determined that Canada's motor vehicle tariff scheme and quota allocations unfairly handicap US auto manufacturers compared to competitors from other foreign nations. 

Also Read | Hacker Steals USD 340 Million in Bitcoin Heist and Returns Most Funds; Know What Happened.

The second directive modifies the scope of Canadian products subject to additional duties according to value, aimed at offsetting restrictions on American alcoholic beverages. The policy adjusts which Canadian goods face penalty tariffs in response to Canadian provincial rules that restrict the distribution, retailing, and purchase of US beer, wine, and spirits.

The third directive enforces an outright import exclusion on select Canadian dairy items entering the US market. The White House highlighted Canada's tariff-rate quota administration on cheeses as an unreasonable trade barrier that disadvantages American dairy farmers.

The fourth directive imposes an explicit import exclusion on designated Canadian alcoholic beverages. This action bans specific Canadian alcohol shipments from entering the country to counter ongoing provincial restrictions that target US liquor products while permitting imports from other international markets.

The fifth directive alters the scope of Canadian goods subject to additional duties related to the ongoing motor vehicle dispute. This order adjusts the targeted list of Canadian exports facing secondary duties to ensure US commercial disadvantages in the automotive industry are fully offset.

The White House noted that additional tariffs under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 were initially scheduled for August 19, 2026, but were temporarily paused for three days following Canadian commitments to resolve the disputes.

However, the administration stated that Canada reneged on its agreement and ceased good-faith negotiations on August 21, 2026, prompting the immediate implementation of both modified duties and direct import exclusions.

Earlier in the day, Trump said that he has ordered federal agencies to stop buying Canadian products through the government's main purchasing catalogue until Ottawa provides equal market access to American businesses and farmers.

The directive orders the General Services Administration (GSA) and the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to immediately begin removing Canadian goods from federal purchasing channels, fueling the ongoing trade dispute between Washington and Ottawa.

In a post on Truth Social, President Trump accused Canada of unfair trade practices, claiming that Canadian federal and local governments block American small businesses from selling to their public sector while Canadian companies enjoy open access to US government contracts.

Declaring a policy of "NO RECIPROCITY – NO ACCESS!", President Trump stated that Canadian goods will remain banned from US government supply lists until Ottawa grants equal market access to American businesses and farmers. 

Trump's remarks come after Canada's retaliatory tariffs targeting US merchandise officially came into force shortly after midnight on Tuesday, as Prime Minister Mark Carney ramped up economic measures against the nation's primary trading partner following the breakdown of bilateral negotiations last month, deepening a prolonged 18-month trade dispute. (ANI)

news.title: Animated Satire "South Park" Changes Name In Dig At Trump
news.text: Animated satire "South Park" said Tuesday it was changing its name to "South America," in an apparent dig at US President Donald Trump's bid to rename swathes of the world.The announcement from the Emmy Award-winning show comes after Trump's recent efforts to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America and the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America.Following the order by Trump, who has also mused about changing the US state of New Mexico to New America, both Apple and Google altered the way the bodies of water are labelled for US users of their maps -- something show creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone took aim at."Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA," said the show's official X account.The pair also took a shot at Paramount, which is now owned by David Ellison's Skydance Corporation, despite the reported $1.5 billion deal they signed last year."We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount -- a Skydance Capitulation," the account wrote.The show customarily known as "South Park" is set in small-town America and known for crude language and lampooning hot-button social issues. Since Trump's return to the White House, it has mercilessly poked fun at him and routinely depicts him as being in a loveless marriage with Satan, while a toady JD Vance plots to evict the devil from the matrimonial bed.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)
news.summary: The announcement from the Emmy Award-winning show comes after Trump's recent efforts to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America and the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America.
